sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive rotation and energy dominance are reshaping the market as Technology slips and Real Estate emerges as the sole sector with clean, multi-horizon positive breadth.

The market is undergoing a clear rotation toward defensive and value-oriented sectors. Energy has claimed the top spot after gaining two positions over the last five sessions, supported by robust momentum of 0.67. Real Estate has quietly established itself as the most fundamentally stable sector, standing as the only group out of 11 to achieve "all-green" status across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD horizons.

Conversely, growth and cyclical sectors are losing their grip. Technology, while still holding the highest absolute momentum score of 0.78, has slipped one spot in rank. The sharpest declines are concentrated in Basic Materials, which tumbled three spots, and Healthcare, which fell two spots, signaling a broader retreat from these areas.

## Strength
* **Real Estate Standout:** Real Estate (momentum 0.55) is the sole "all-green" sector in the market, showing positive performance across the week, month, quarter, half-year, and YTD.
* **Energy Dominance:** Energy has surged to the #1 YTD rank, backed by strong momentum of 0.67.
* **Tech's Absolute Lead:** Technology maintains the highest absolute momentum score at 0.783, despite its recent ranking slip.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Defensive Gainers:** Utilities (+2 spots, rank 6, momentum 0.55) and Consumer Defensive (+1 spots, rank 5, momentum 0.38) are climbing the ranks.
* **Sharpest Decliners:** Basic Materials fell 3 spots to rank 7 (momentum 0.25), while Healthcare dropped 2 spots to rank 9 (momentum 0.48).
* **Persistent Laggards:** Consumer Cyclical remains anchored at the bottom of the YTD rankings (rank 11) with a weak momentum score of 0.283.

## Divergences
* **Technology Fading:** Technology exhibits a bearish divergence, with its rank slipping by 1 spot over the last 5 sessions despite maintaining a high momentum score of 0.78.
* **Financials Disconnect:** Financials hold a relatively strong momentum score of 0.583, yet they remain weighed down at rank 8 YTD.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and defensive sectors are surging as Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing claims the top momentum spot, while aerospace, airlines, and clean energy face sharp weekly declines.

The market is showing a clear shift toward energy and defensive value. Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing leads the charge as the top overall momentum performer, supported by a broader rotation into energy spaces like Oil & Gas E&P and Integrated Oil & Gas, which both jumped over 20 rank spots this week. Healthcare Plans and Consumer Electronics also maintain robust "all-green" status, showing sustained strength across all time horizons.

Conversely, high-flying and growth-oriented sectors are fading rapidly. Aerospace & Defense plummeted 27 spots, while Airlines and clean energy niches like Solar and Uranium experienced steep weekly rank declines. Meanwhile, consumer-facing areas like Discount Stores and Restaurants are beginning to quietly climb the ranks despite currently depressed momentum scores.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** Only 16 of 144 industry groups maintain all-green status across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD frames, led by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.97 momentum) and Healthcare Plans (0.87 momentum).
* **Sustained Leaders:** Computer Hardware (0.89 momentum, YTD rank 1) and Financial Conglomerates (0.84 momentum) join Refining and Healthcare Plans as the market's most resilient multi-month anchors.
* **Defensive Real Estate:** REIT - Healthcare Facilities (0.79 momentum) remains a key pillar of sustained strength, holding its position in the top 36 industries across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Energy Surge:** Chemicals (+23 spots to rank 24), Oil & Gas E&P (+22 spots to rank 32), and Oil & Gas Integrated (+20 spots to rank 23) dominated the weekly leaderboard.
* **Employment & Utilities:** Staffing & Employment Services climbed 20 spots to rank 30 with strong 0.79 momentum, while Utilities - Regulated Gas jumped 16 spots to rank 65.
* **Severe Laggards:** Pharmaceutical Retailers (0.06 momentum, YTD rank 144) and Mortgage Finance (0.18 momentum, YTD rank 143) remain anchored to the bottom of the market.
* **Sharpest Decliners:** Aerospace & Defense fell 27 spots to rank 86, while Airlines dropped 20 spots and Solar shed 19 spots.

## Divergences
* **Fading Momentum:** Airlines (0.61 momentum) and Biotechnology (0.68 momentum) are showing early warning signs, dropping 20 and 11 rank spots respectively over the last 5 sessions.
* **Emerging from the Bottom:** Discount Stores (+12 spots, 0.43 momentum) and Restaurants (+10 spots, 0.46 momentum) are beginning to rotate upward despite their low overall momentum scores.
* **Commodity Contrast:** While Uranium (-19 spots) and Silver (-17 spots) are plunging, Thermal Coal is quietly emerging, rising 9 spots this week on low 0.33 momentum.
